comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment of repurchase and resale agreements
comparisons.peer_summary: Securities sold under agreements to repurchase (repos) and purchased under agreements to resell (reverse repos) are treated as collateralized financing transactions rather than sales or purchases of the underlying securities.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C discuss the accounting treatment of securities financing transactions. MS specifically lists the components included in its interest tables (interest on repos/resales, fees on borrowed/loaned securities). C similarly identifies these exact transaction types (repos, reverse repos, securities borrowed/loaned) and clarifies that for accounting purposes, they are treated as collateralized financing transactions rather than sales or purchases of underlying securities, which provides the context for how the associated interest and fees are recognized.

Securities sold under agreements to repurchase (repos) and securities purchased under agreements to resell (reverse repos) do not constitute a sale (or purchase) of the underlying securities for accounting purposes and are treated as collateralized financing transactions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Presentation of Financial Instruments on Consolidated Balance Sheets
comparisons.peer_summary: Derivatives are reported on a net-by-counterparty basis when enforceable netting agreements exist and net of cash collateral under enforceable credit support agreements; however, resale/repurchase and securities borrowing/loaning transactions are not reported net of collateral.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the presentation and netting of resale/repurchase and securities borrowing/loaning transactions. MS defines the specific interest and fee components included in its interest tables related to these transactions (e.g., interest paid on securities purchased under agreements to resell, fees paid on securities borrowed). GS discusses the balance sheet presentation, noting that these same transaction types (resale, repurchase, borrowed, loaned) are presented on a net-by-counterparty basis when specific settlement and netting criteria are met, but are not reported net of collateral. Both confirm the standard use of these instruments in their financing activities.

sentences.text: 2.Includes interest paid on Securities purchased under agreements to resell.

Resale agreements and securities sold under agreements to repurchase (repurchase agreements) and securities borrowed and loaned transactions with the same settlement date are presented on a net-by-counterparty basis in the consolidated balance sheets when such transactions meet certain settlement criteria and are subject to netting agreements.
In the consolidated balance sheets, resale and repurchase agreements, and securities borrowed and loaned, are not reported net of the related cash and securities received or posted as collateral.

comparisons.peer_summary: Further information on accounting for interest income and expense related to hedge accounting, investment securities, securities financing activities, loans, and long-term debt is available in Notes 5, 10, 11, 12, and 20.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM explicitly link their interest income/expense disclosures to their securities financing activities. MS itemizes the interest and fees included in its interest tables that arise from securities borrowed, loaned, and agreements to resell/repurchase. JPM cross-references Note 11 and Note 12 for further information on interest income and expense related to securities financing activities, specifically defining these activities as 'securities purchased or sold under resale or repurchase agreements; securities borrowed; and securities loaned,' mirroring the components MS lists.
